_comment: Montezuma's Revenge (Atari 2600) RAM map. Addresses below are the COMMONLY CITED ones from the RL / Go-Explore literature. They are a STARTING POINT — every address has verify=false until you confirm it against your own ALE/BizHawk session (drive a known input and watch the byte move the way you expect). 2600 RAM is 128 bytes, addresses 0x00-0x7F (0-127).

room.note: current room id. CONSISTENT (stayed 1 in all captures) but UNCONFIRMED — Joe never left room 1, so a transition was never observed. Re-confirm by walking through a door.

x.note: CONFIRMED. Panama Joe X. +1/frame under RIGHT, -1 under LEFT. RAM-x ≈ screen-x (scale≈1.0, offset≈-1).

y.note: CONFIRMED. Panama Joe Y, but INVERTED: RAM-y INCREASES upward (jump raised it 235->252). screen_y = C - ram_y; C still unpinned.

lives.note: CONFIRMED-ish. Decremented 5->4->3 as Joe died during random play. Value = spare lives remaining.

level.note: level number (pyramid resets harder each level). CONFIRM.

items.note: inventory bitmask (key/sword/torch/amulet). Pick up a key and watch a bit flip. CONFIRM.

orb_count_or_score_lo.note: score is BCD across a few bytes — CONFIRM range by scoring.

enemy_candidates._comment: Enemies (skull, snakes, spiders, laser barriers) have position + an animation/movement timer byte each. These are UNKNOWN — find them by diffing RAM while only an enemy moves and the player stands still.

calibration._comment: Fill these after running the logger with --calibrate. Solve screen_px = scale*ram + offset per axis using two known reference positions (e.g. left wall, right wall).

x.note: from walk capture + frame diff; RAM-x≈screen-x

y.note: PINNED: screen_row = 287 - 0.85*ram_y. Fitted from 6 walk frames. RAM-y inverted (up = larger) and ~1.18x finer than pixels.

native_frame.note: ALE getScreenRGB() resolution. Author the gym-gen game in this space, then scale up uniformly.

ale_action_ids._comment: ALE full action set (Discrete(18)) used to DRIVE capture. Distinct from the gym-gen Discrete(8) the final game exposes.
